Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

grand adjective

magnificent, splendid

also magnificent, grandiose, sumptuous, imposing

classical

Cic. Leg. 2.1.2: magnificae vīllae (Lewis & Short)

magnificus, magnifica, magnificum

adjective; comparative magnificentior, superlative magnificentissimus

grand, magnificent, sumptuous

Of houses, dinners, funerals, games and deeds: grand, splendid, costly. Of a person it means high-minded, or fond of display (Sall. C. 9; Nep. Att. 13); in Plautus, boastful (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • splendidus, splendida, splendidum — splendid; of a way of living, sumptuous

    also used · classical · Cic. Par. 38: quōrum in vīllā ac domō nihil splendidum fuit praeter ipsōs (Lewis & Short)

    First bright, shining; then splendid in dress and way of living, and of people distinguished (Lewis & Short).

  • amplus, ampla, amplum — large and imposing; of rank, distinguished

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.139: ampla domus dēdecorī dominō fit, sī est in eā sōlitūdō (Lewis & Short)

    Grand as spacious and stately: a house, honours, a funeral; the superlative amplissimus is Cicero’s word for men of the highest rank (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • atque omne ignōtum prō magnificō est

    and everything unknown is taken for something grandTac. Agr. 30.4

  • ampla domus dēdecorī dominō fit, sī est in eā sōlitūdō

    a grand house is a disgrace to its master if it stands emptyCic. Off. 1.139 (Lewis & Short)

See also big, wonderful, great.
